newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals quiet, seek direction.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals quiet, seek direction.

text.p: The precious metals drifted quietly in early trading on Tuesday, awaiting market direction in the aftermath of recent price upheavals.
"The gold market does not have a strong opinion of where it is going. It's pretty nervous and people are trying to be as flat as possible," a dealer said.
Bullion was fixed at $368.80 an ounce, little changed from Monday's afternoon fixing of $369.00 and a London close of $368.70/$369.20.
Prices moved up about $1.00 from lower overnight levels in early trading as bullion houses squared their books for fear of being caught short of the market, dealers said.
However, a bearish mood prevailed with expectations pinned on an eventual dip to $360 an ounce.
The market has been jumpy against a backdrop of sharp falls in recent weeks and a strong but short-lived rally sparked by heavy losses in financial markets last Friday.
"Last week got very busy and people were caught short and bought at the highs. With the Christmas period usually quiet it took everyone by surprise," the dealer said.

Analysts say gold is more likely to head lower than recover in the near term, with selling by producers seen capping any rally attempts and seasonal demand for the metal lower than expected this year.
Silver prices also ticked up on the back of gold and was indicated two cents up from Monday's London close at $4.80/$4.82 an ounce.
Platinum was also little changed from Monday's London closing levels, indicated at $368.00/$369.00 an ounce.
Prices had slid to fresh three-year lows on Monday after coming under heavy selling pressure late last week, which dealers said likely originated from investment funds.
"I doubt it's going to go much lower than this right now," a dealer said.
Platinum was at a slight discount to gold, which investors usually considered a signal to buy the metal, he added.
